faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Answers to the questions I'm asked most often before a project starts.

items.question: Why not build the application myself with an AI or no-code tool?
items.answer: They are great for prototyping. The hard part comes next: connecting your software, handling permissions and edge cases, migrating your data, fixing things without breaking others. If such a tool is enough, I will tell you.

items.question: How long will it take to build my project?
items.answer: A few days for a usable prototype, several weeks in increments for a full business application. The quote sets out a stage-by-stage schedule.

items.question: How do you put a quote together?
items.answer: After a first conversation, I write a short specification and a quote broken down by batch: scope, deliverables, schedule and price.

items.question: Who owns the code and the accounts?
items.answer: Yours: code, repositories, hosting, domain names and service accounts are in your name, documentation included.

items.question: Do you take care of hosting and maintenance?
items.answer: Yes if you want it: deployment, monitoring, alerts and backups, or a rollout on your own infrastructure.

items.question: Do you work remotely or on site?
items.answer: Both: remotely anywhere in France, and on site around Toulouse when it helps.

items.question: Can you take over an existing application?
items.answer: Yes. I start with a review of the code and the data, then propose a gradual evolution rather than a risky rewrite.

items.question: What role does AI play, and does my code stay confidential?
items.answer: AI speeds up execution; I design, I review and I stay responsible. No secret is handed to it, and the code stays in your repositories.

rows.mine: Tests first, tooled acceptance testing, evidence in production

frame.title: Scope before generating
frame.description: The need becomes versioned specs, split into deliverables with acceptance criteria. One contract per repository sets the rules.
frame.proof: A 28-deliverable roadmap drove the SSO rollout across 9 applications.

orchestrate.title: Orchestrate
orchestrate.description: A plan approved before any code, specialized sub-agents, effort calibrated to risk, worktrees to parallelize without conflict.
orchestrate.proof: A fresh session executes what another one planned, to remove confirmation bias.

guard.title: Set guardrails
guard.description: Deterministic hooks, restricted permissions, no secret handed to AI. Autonomy is bounded, human escalation explicit.
guard.proof: Guardrails are technical, not just instructions.

prove.title: Prove it
prove.description: Failing tests first, then multi-agent testing in a real browser. Every verdict is re-measured and the evidence is kept.
prove.proof: 5 campaigns, over 800 cases, up to 11 agents in parallel.

decide.title: Keep the final say
decide.description: Every change reviewed, architecture and security calls made by me. No code I do not understand gets merged.
decide.proof: I remain accountable for what goes to production.

capitalize.title: Capitalize and stay ahead
capitalize.description: Reusable skills, a registry of pitfalls, a wiki updated in the same patch, long-term memory shared between agents.
capitalize.proof: Active watch: agentic engineering, spec-driven development, MCP, Claude Code and Codex updates.
